prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a small indoor corner room with a recessed wall shelf on the right (about 1 to 1.8 metres away), wall-mounted bags at eye level on the left wall (about 1.2 to 2 metres away), and floor vessels below (1.5 to 2.2 metres away). In frames 1 and 2, a bare-chested man on the right stands 0.5 to 1.2 metres in front of the camera wearer facing away toward the shelf within his arm's reach, while a second man on the far left stands about 0.8 to 1.2 metres away facing right (roughly 1 metre from the right-hand man) before dropping mostly out of view to a single hand in frame 2. Across frames 3 and 4, the camera wearer steps closer to the shelf (within 0.6 to 1 metre) and extends their own right arm into the foreground (0.2 to 0.6 metres) to reach the upper shelf alongside the right-hand man, whose head and torso become heavily cropped and occluded at the right edge. In frame 5, the camera wearer turns left, placing the first man's face and torso at the extreme left edge within 0.3 metres, while the camera wearer's outstretched right arm holds a small cup at 0.4 to 0.7 metres and a third man stands in the background 2 to 2.5 metres away facing and looking toward the camera wearer. The depth map clearly separates the foreground silhouettes of the extended arms, hanging bags, and shelf recess edge that blend into shadows in the RGB image, but it is unreliable in frame 5 where the background man standing 2 metres away is rendered nearly pitch black as if infinitely far, and in frames 3 and 4 where fine shelf objects merge into flat grey planes.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates selected people and small containers across the five frames while leaving the room walls, recessed shelf structure, and most floor items unlabelled in black. In frames 1 and 2, it segments the man on the left (about 0.8 to 1.2 metres away, cropped at the left border) and the man on the right (0.5 to 1.2 metres away, facing the shelf with his back to the camera), along with a metal pot on the floor between them (~1.8 metres away, labelled 'bowl') and a bottle on the upper shelf (~1.2 metres away, within the right-hand man's arm's reach). In frames 3 and 4, as the camera approaches the shelf and the wearer's right arm reaches up into the foreground (0.3 to 0.7 metres away) next to the right-hand man, both the wearer's reaching arm and the adjacent man are merged or split across adjacent 'person' masks, while the upper-shelf bottle (~0.8 metres away) and the hanging plastic bag to its left (~1 metre away) are segmented. In frame 5, as the camera turns left, the map segments the very close man on the far left (<0.3 metres, partly out of view), the standing man behind him (~2 to 2.5 metres away, facing and looking toward the camera wearer while holding a red bag), the teal backpack hanging on the right wall (~1.5 metres away), and a floor vessel below (~1.8 metres away, labelled 'cup'/'bowl'). This map makes it easy to track the exact 2D boundaries of the upper-shelf bottle and foreground silhouettes against cluttered backgrounds, but it is highly unreliable in misclassifying the hanging white plastic bag as a 'bottle' in frames 2 to 4, merging the camera wearer's arm with the adjacent person in frame 3, fragmenting the person mask in frame 4, and completely missing the camera wearer's outstretched right arm and handheld cup in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D yellow body keypoints and torso links on a black background, completely omitting all room geometry, objects, and magenta hand skeletons across all five frames. In frame 1 and frame 4, no skeletons are detected at all despite two people standing within 0.5 to 1.2 metres of the camera wearer and active foreground hands reaching toward the shelf. In frame 2, a single torso rectangle, left upper arm, and cluster of head keypoints capture the man standing ~1 metre in front of the camera wearer on the right, showing his back turned toward the camera and his head angled toward the shelf within his arm's reach. In frame 3, only a partial upper-body linkage and two separate clusters of head keypoints are detected at the right side (about 0.5 to 0.8 metres away), reflecting the close proximity and mutual occlusion of the man at the shelf and the camera wearer's reaching arm. In frame 5, a full upper-body torso rectangle with both arms and facial keypoints appears in the upper left for the standing man ~2 to 2.5 metres away, clearly showing his frontal orientation and gaze directed toward the camera wearer even against the dim background, while thepose map remains unreliable for close-range egocentric spatial layout because it misses the very close man at the left edge (<0.3 metres), all cropped bodies in frames 1 and 4, and every foreground hand within arm's reach.
